questions.q: Track Changes in MS Word is found under which tab?
questions.solution: Track Changes, Comments, Compare, Protect and Word Count are all on the Review tab.
questions.shortcut: Anything about checking/editing text collectively lives in Review.

questions.q: Which port carries digital audio and video signals over a single cable to a monitor or TV?
questions.solution: HDMI transmits uncompressed digital video plus audio in one cable. VGA is analog video-only, PS/2 is for keyboard/mouse, and serial COM ports carry slow bit-serial data.
questions.shortcut: Audio AND video together -> HDMI (or DisplayPort, if listed).

questions.q: The port that transmits data one bit at a time as a single stream, traditionally used for slow data over long distances, is the:
questions.solution: A serial port (COM/RS-232) sends bits sequentially over one channel - slower but reliable over longer cable runs. Parallel ports send a byte across 8 wires simultaneously but only over short distances.
questions.shortcut: 'One bit at a time / single stream' = serial, word for word.

questions.q: Which key combination ends a running slide show?
questions.solution: Esc exits the slideshow back to the editor (Alt+F4 would close PowerPoint itself; F5 starts a show).
questions.shortcut: Presenting runs until Escape - the universal cancel key.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To bite the bullet
options: to endure a painful situation bravely
questions.solution: Soldiers once bit a bullet during surgery without anaesthesia — **to bear pain with courage**. 'To give up easily' inverts the meaning; the rest are literal.
questions.shortcut: Old surgery picture → brave endurance.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the author's overall approach in the passage?
options: Alarmed and fatalistic about the future of cities
Informative analysis combined with guarded optimism about remedies
Strictly neutral, presenting data without any judgement
questions.solution: The author explains causes, documents unequal harm (concerned, informative), then presents workable measures and a model plan, closing on 'can plan itself out of one' (guarded optimism). (a) fails — the closing is hopeful, not fatalistic. (c) — the passage criticises no one and uses no mockery. (d) — the author clearly evaluates solutions, so 'strictly neutral' misreads the final paragraph.
questions.shortcut: Tone = direction + degree. Problem + solvable ending ⇒ concerned-but-optimistic; the last sentence settles it.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (2).
questions.solution: The clauses move in opposite directions — the walk demands nothing (+), yet few sustain it (−). Contrast is required: **yet**. *So/hence* would wrongly make continuation scarce a *result* of the walk's simplicity; *because* reverses the logic entirely.
questions.shortcut: + clause, − clause → contrast word (yet/but).

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A place where bees are kept
questions.solution: Bees are kept in an **apiary**; *aviary* (one letter away) keeps birds, *aquarium* fish, *granary* grain.
questions.shortcut: Stored-object anchor; the aviary trap is deliberate.

questions.q: **Madhubani** painting, traditionally drawn by women of the Mithila region, belongs to —
questions.solution: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is from **Bihar**, marked by double-line borders and natural colours. It has a GI tag. Odisha's scroll art is Pattachitra.
questions.shortcut: Mithila → Madhubani district → Bihar.

questions.q: The **Poona Pact (1932)** on the representation of the depressed classes was signed between —
questions.solution: After the **Communal Award** (1932), Gandhi fasted in Yerawada jail. The **Poona Pact** with **B.R. Ambedkar** replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.
questions.shortcut: Poona Pact = depressed-class seats → Ambedkar.

questions.q: The first **Jnanpith Award** (1965) went to G. Sankara Kurup, who wrote in —
questions.solution: **G. Sankara Kurup** received the first Jnanpith for his **Malayalam** poetry collection *Odakkuzhal* ('The Bamboo Flute').
questions.shortcut: First Jnanpith = Kerala poet Kurup.

questions.q: The method of election of the President of India and the Directive Principles of State Policy have been borrowed from which country?
questions.solution: Both the DPSP and the method of electing the President (indirect election through an electoral college) were taken from the **Constitution of Ireland**. Ireland also gave the provision for nominating 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.
questions.shortcut: Ireland = 'President + Principles' — both P-words pair up.

questions.q: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 14 cm and 10 cm, and the distance between them is 8 cm. Its area is:
questions.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 260 160" width="260" stroke="currentColor" fill="none"><polygon points="40,130 220,130 170,40 90,40" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="130" y1="40" x2="130" y2="130" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><text x="30" y="150" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">a</text><text x="214" y="150" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">b</text><text x="136" y="90" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">h</text></svg>
questions.solution: $K=\frac12(a+b)h=\frac12\times24\times8=96$ sq cm.
questions.shortcut: Sum 24, half is 12, ×8 = 96. Trap: 192 missed the half.

questions.q: Two trains, each 200 m long, run in the same direction at 72 km/h and 54 km/h. The time the faster train takes to completely cross the slower one is:
questions.solution:
$S_{\text{rel}} = 72 - 54 = 18$ km/h $= 5$ m/s (same direction ⇒ subtract).
Combined length $= 400$ m ⇒ $t = \frac{400}{5} = 80$ seconds.
questions.shortcut: Same direction ⇒ subtract: 5 m/s; both lengths: 400/5 = 80 s.

questions.q: For a firm in 2022, income was ₹6.6 crore and expenditure ₹5.5 crore. The profit percentage is:
questions.shortcut: $\frac{1.1}{5.5}=\frac15\to20\%$. Profit percent is always on **expenditure**.

questions.q: The total surface area of a cuboid of dimensions $8\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ is:
questions.shortcut: Half of 208 is 104 — the bracket sum; double it. Trap: 104 (no doubling).

questions.q:
**Statement:** Doctors advise that adults should sleep for at least seven hours a night to stay healthy.

**Conclusions:**
I. Sleeping for more than seven hours a night is harmful for adults.
II. Regularly sleeping for less than seven hours may affect an adult's health.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: I invents a harm from sleeping more — the advice sets a minimum, not a maximum — **does not follow**. II is the direct implication of 'at least seven hours to stay healthy' and is suitably soft ('may') — **follows**. Answer: **Only II**.
questions.shortcut: 'At least' sets a floor; it says nothing about going above it.

questions.q: Five people **A, B, C, D and E sit around a circular table facing the centre. E sits between C and B (immediately), D sits immediately to the left of B, and A sits to the immediate right of C.** Who sits **second to the right of B**?
questions.solution: Facing centre: left = clockwise. From C clockwise: E (between C and B), then B, then D at B's left. A sits at C's right (anticlockwise), closing the circle. Clockwise: A, C, E, B, D. Second to the right of B = two anticlockwise = **C**.
questions.shortcut: 'Between' + 'immediate left' chains trace the clockwise order almost by themselves.
